brief: A Staffordshire porcelain spaniel half-swaddled in bubble wrap, lying in an open moving box on kraft-brown cardboard. Every air dome is its own small lens, so the dog's glazed cheek and gilt collar are magnified, split and doubled from cell to cell. The medium is transparent watercolour, glazed layer on layer in raw sienna, bone white and cool polythene grey. Crisp opaque white pen dots catch the highlight on every dome. Taped seams stay matte. Corrugated cardboard edges are drawn in sharp pencil. The frame is cropped tight and slightly off-axis, like a phone snapshot taken mid-unpacking.

A bicycle leaning against an iron railing at dawn, shot close on the saddle and top tube. Every surface is furred with feathery hoarfrost needles, drawn as countless fine white pencil and pen spikes radiating from edges. They cluster thickest on the stitching and brake cable. The ground is cold blue-grey toned paper. The cracked leather and chipped British-racing-green paint show through in muted coloured pencil. A thin wash of pale apricot sunrise touches one side only, where a few needles have begun to glisten.

A hyperreal heap of clear plastic gacha capsules spills across a perfectly flat bubblegum-pink field with no horizon or floor shadow. Inside each half-domed shell sits a tiny glossy figurine: a cat, a dumpling, a bunny. Every capsule seam, mould mark and specular glint is rendered with obsessive marker precision. The background is deadpan flat, with even sticker-like outlines in thin black ink. Accents of mint, butter yellow and baby blue repeat rhythmically across the pile, so the image is both a product photograph and an anime wallpaper.

A stereoscope card on a buff mount with arched windows holds two near-identical views side by side, each a hyperreal fried egg in a cast-iron skillet. The views differ by a slight shift in angle, so the yolk's glossy dome and the lacy browned whites seem ready to pop forward. The images are rendered in graphite and sepia wash, with fine pencil hatching for the seasoned iron and crisp white gouache-like gleams on the yolk. The card has a printed caption, rounded corners, foxing spots and one creased corner.

A hyperreal close portrait of a sleeping young man, cheek pressed into a pillow, rendered entirely in ultramarine. Deep velvety charcoal-like masses build the shadows of eye socket, lip and ear, through Prussian blue, ultramarine and pale cornflower. Breathing-soft gradations model the skin. A fine sprinkle of metallic gold spray settles across the face and pillowcase like pyrite flecks in polished stone. Faint pale-grey calcite veins drift across the background. Nothing has an outline; the face exists purely through pigment density.

A single page from a vintage alphabet primer. A huge serif capital Y and a lowercase y, printed in faded tomato red, sit at the top left of cream laid paper. Beneath them hangs a wooden yo-yo, twirling slightly, rendered in hyperreal burnished coloured pencil. You can see the grain of the varnished maple, a chipped edge, and a frayed twisted cotton string with every fibre. A simple stamped-ink frame encloses the scene, its corners worn. The captioned word "yo-yo" sits below in crisp schoolbook type. The palette is vermilion, ochre and pencil-grey on aged paper.

Three uncapped felt-tip pens lie on a damp circle of laboratory filter paper. Each barrel, cap clip and printed brand logo is rendered with hyperreal plastic sheen in pencil and watercolour. From each nib the ink climbs and separates into concentric rings: black splits into cerulean, rose madder and lemon. Brown fans out into violet and saffron. The bands meet with wet blooms and feathered capillary edges. A hard pale tidemark rings the outermost front. The viewpoint is close, the paper buckled, and cool fluorescent lab-bench light falls from above.

A hyperreal overhead view of an unmade bed in rumpled white linen, rendered entirely with even-pressure contour lines like a weather chart. Concentric lines tighten around deep creases and spread wide across flat sheet. The low pressure of a pillow hollow becomes a nest of tight rings. A few cold-front and warm-front marks run along major folds in soft cerulean and rose pencil. Shading emerges only from line density. The ground is pale grey-blue paper. The mood is analytical yet intimate, morning-still.

A hand-knitted mustard cardigan lies across a striped canvas deckchair on a lawn edge, captured as an early colour plate. Everything is built from dense stippled grains of orange-red, violet and green, which blend optically into soft, faintly shimmering colour. Stitch structure, a dangling loose thread and the deckchair's weathered wooden frame are resolved with patient precision, yet the whole surface hums with grainy luminosity. Shadows go plum-brown, highlights are warm and powdery, and the vignetted corners darken gently.

An empty municipal swimming pool seen from the deep end looking up the chrome ladder and tiled steps. Drain grates, hairline tile cracks and a dry leaf are rendered with photographic exactness. The whole image is built from granular rosin-dust tone: soft spray grain stopped out in stages, so deep umber shadows step up through warm greys to paper-white highlights on the rails. Fine etched hatching sharpens the tile grid. A plate-tone margin and a bevelled platemark frame the image, which has the silent, still atmosphere of an off-season afternoon.

A folded batik sarong lies on a teak bench, rendered with full photographic depth in watercolour resist. Its soga brown, indigo and ivory parang pattern bends correctly over every fold and tuck. The signature wax crackle runs through the indigo as fine dark veins wherever the cloth creases. Reserved pale lines are left as untouched paper. Dyes pool and soften at seams. A brass canting tool and a curl of cold beeswax rest on top, sharp-edged and glinting. Warm, low, late-afternoon light rakes in from one side.

A split pomegranate rendered hyperreal yet jewel-like. The leathery rind is treated as translucent ruby enamel over a fine guilloché pattern of engraved waves, glowing from beneath in layered transparent washes. The exposed arils are faceted cabochons of garnet and pigeon-blood red, each with a crisp starburst highlight. The membrane is pale pearl, the crown is chased gold, and seed pearls are dotted along the cut edge. It sits on a deep imperial-blue velvet cushion. Lighting is a soft jeweller's spotlight. Opulent, precise and ceremonious.

A jarring collage of hyperreal fragments, each rendered in meticulous graphite as if it had been cut from a photograph. A grinning mouth with one gold crown, half a pocket watch with its movement exposed, a bowler-hatted ear and a pair of pliers. The torn paper edges are left raw and white, and the pieces are pasted at clashing angles and scales. Scraps of red-and-black stencil lettering and newsprint hatching sit between them. The ground is grey kraft, and one flat vermilion disc is slapped across the middle. The arrangement is deliberately unbalanced, top-heavy and confrontational.

A crank-handled desk pencil sharpener shown in an exploded view, like a patent sheet. Gears, burr cylinders, the clamp and the crank float apart along dashed axis lines, all in even-weight black technical pen with leader lines and fig. lettering. One part breaks the convention: the shavings-filled receptacle is rendered in hyperreal graphite, with curled cedar shavings, flecks of yellow lacquer and smeared lead dust. The rest stays cold diagrammatic line on stiff white bristol. The view is asymmetric and sprawls across the sheet toward the lower right.

A savoy cabbage sliced in half, its cut face shown in hyperreal detail. The concentric leaf layers read as malachite banding, in looping bands of viridian, deep bottle green, mint and nearly black, laid in crisp-edged watercolour with fine pen dividing lines. Moisture beads on the cut surface as sharp white highlights, and the outer crinkled leaves are rendered in hyperreal detail with every blister and vein. It rests on a cold slate board, and the composition is shoved hard to one side, as though the slab had just been cut and polished.

A silver Ethiopian hand cross lies across a folded goatskin, framed inside bold manuscript borders of interlaced bands in red ochre, leaf green and saffron. The borders are flat marker fills with confident black pen contours. Inside the frame the cross is hyperreal: tarnished filigree lattices, scratches and a worn leather thong. The vellum is rendered just as precisely, with hair follicles and a buckled surface. The flat, sacred, frontal decorative frame contains an obsessively observed object, and a column of rhythmic red-and-black script runs down one side.

A domed resin paperweight holds a suspended dandelion seed head, shown in deep honey and cognac tones. Layered warm watercolour glazes build depth from pale citrine at the dome's crown to treacly burnt sienna at the base. Trapped air bubbles, hairline stress fractures and a few drifting detached seeds are drawn in delicate pen and lifted highlights. The parachute filaments are hyperreal white pencil threads. A heavy refracted shadow pools gold on a dark walnut desk, and the whole sphere glows from within.

A crumpled linen napkin on a bare oak table, built the way a monotype is: the sheet begins as a dense slab of lamp-black charcoal mass, and the cloth is pulled out of the dark by wiping and lifting. Highlights are rag-smears and fingertip lifts with soft ghosted borders. Folds have a slightly doubled, offset edge like an uneven press. Hyperreal weave texture appears only where light catches the crests. Warm bone-white against brown-black, with a faint bloom of burnt umber where ink pooled. The napkin sits low and off-left, with a heavy margin of plate tone above it.

A jungle crow perched on a sagging utility wire against a field of crushed azurite blue. The sky is laid in granular, sparkling watercolour that settles into gritty mineral texture. A tarnished gold-leaf mist band drifts behind the bird. The feathers are hyperreal, with iridescent oil-slick sheen in malachite green and violet built from fine layered pencil over dense ink-black mass. The beak shows scuffs and the eye has a wet highlight. The wire and an insulator are rendered with industrial precision, and the bird sits high-right in a vast, quiet expanse.

An open human palm, facing up, fills a sheet of buff paper. Its whole form is described through continuous graphite contour lines, like elevation rings, that circle the thenar mound and fingertip pads and crowd tightly in the deep creases. A heavier index line falls on every fifth ring. Where the lines are densest, hyperreal skin detail emerges: dermal ridges, a callus and a splinter. Faint survey ticks and elevation numerals in red pencil sit near the margins without forming legible values. The hand is cropped at the wrist, off-centre and top-lit.
